meta.name: Integration Landscape Catalogue
meta.purpose: Deterministic description of the integration surface around a commerce platform: interfaces, end-to-end flows, field mappings, API contracts and the file patterns that link a code change to each of them.
meta.generalizationPolicy: Client-specific names are normalised to architectural roles. Nothing here contains source code, business logic, credentials or captured production data. Sample payloads are illustrative.

_comment_topologies: A landscape is described by which of these it uses, not by assuming one. A customer with no middleware simply has no MIDDLEWARE profile enabled, and every module downstream stops mentioning one.

topologies.label: Middleware-mediated
topologies.description: Commerce exchanges messages with an integration platform, which transforms and routes them to the target system. Common with SAP Integration Suite (CPI), MuleSoft, Boomi or webMethods.

stageChain.label: Commerce
stageChain.detail: Business event or API call originates in the commerce platform.

stageChain.label: Payload build
stageChain.detail: Domain model converted to a DTO and serialised to the wire format.

stageChain.label: Transport
stageChain.detail: Message leaves commerce over the configured channel and authentication scheme.

stageChain.label: Integration platform
stageChain.detail: Receives, validates, enriches and routes the message.

stageChain.label: Mapping
stageChain.detail: Source structure mapped to the target structure. The most common source of silent field loss.

stageChain.label: Target system
stageChain.detail: ERP or line-of-business system persists the document and returns a result.

stageChain.label: Acknowledgement
stageChain.detail: Result or error propagated back to commerce.

topologies.label: Direct point-to-point
topologies.description: Commerce calls the target system directly with no middleware hop. Fewer moving parts, but transformation and retry become the caller's problem.

stageChain.label: Commerce
stageChain.detail: Call originates in the commerce platform.

stageChain.label: Payload build
stageChain.detail: Domain model serialised straight into the target system's own contract.

stageChain.label: Transport
stageChain.detail: Direct call, usually synchronous and usually authenticated per-request.

stageChain.label: Target system
stageChain.detail: Target processes the request inline and returns a result.

topologies.label: File exchange
topologies.description: Files are written to or read from a shared location and processed in batches. Very common for price, stock and catalogue feeds, and often the only integration a smaller retailer runs.

stageChain.label: File produced
stageChain.detail: A job writes a delimited or fixed-width file from the source system.

stageChain.label: Transfer
stageChain.detail: File lands on SFTP, an object store or a mounted share.

stageChain.label: Import job
stageChain.detail: A scheduled job parses, validates and applies the rows. Partial success is normal and must be reported per row.

topologies.label: Event streaming
topologies.description: Events are published to a broker and consumed independently. Producers do not know their consumers, so a payload change is a fan-out risk rather than a single-consumer risk.

stageChain.label: Event published
stageChain.detail: Business event emitted by the commerce platform.

stageChain.label: Broker
stageChain.detail: Topic retains the event; consumers read at their own pace.

stageChain.label: Consumers
stageChain.detail: One or more independent consumers process the event.

interfaces.name: Order creation
interfaces.description: Places a confirmed commerce order in the target ERP as a sales order.

interfaces.name: Invoice retrieval
interfaces.description: Fetches invoice headers and documents for an order so a customer can view or download them.

interfaces.name: Shipment tracking
interfaces.description: Reads delivery and tracking status for dispatched orders.

interfaces.name: Pricing simulation
interfaces.description: Asks the ERP to price a basket in real time, including customer-specific conditions.

interfaces.name: Return request
interfaces.description: Raises a return or refund request against a delivered order.

interfaces.name: Product master
interfaces.description: Loads product master data and catalogue attributes into commerce.

interfaces.name: Price conditions
interfaces.description: Loads list and condition prices. Frequently the only integration a file-based landscape runs daily.

interfaces.name: Inventory levels
interfaces.description: Updates available stock per product and plant.

interfaces.name: Customer and business partner
interfaces.description: Synchronises customer accounts and business partner records into commerce.

interfaces.name: Material and plant data
interfaces.description: Loads material master and plant assignments used for availability and fulfilment.

interfaces.name: Customer material info record
interfaces.description: Resolves the customer-specific material number for a product so the customer sees their own part number.

interfaces.name: Order history
interfaces.description: Reads historical orders from the ERP for the account self-service area.

flows.name: Create Order
flows.summary: A confirmed commerce order becomes a sales order in the ERP.

stages.name: Order placed
stages.purpose: The order is confirmed in commerce and becomes eligible for export.
debugTips: Confirm the order reached a state that triggers export, not just a saved state.

stages.name: Convert to DTO
stages.purpose: Converters and populators translate the domain model into a transport DTO. A field that no populator writes is silently absent downstream.

possibleErrors.title: Populator failed on a null attribute
No converter registered for the type

debugTips: Check the populator list for the converter bean — a new field usually needs a new populator, not a converter change.
A field present in the model but absent from the payload almost always means a missing populator.

stages.name: Build payload
stages.purpose: The DTO is serialised to the agreed wire format and envelope.
debugTips: Compare the produced payload against the agreed schema in the Payload Explorer before blaming the receiver.

stages.name: Send to middleware
stages.purpose: The payload is transmitted over the configured channel with the configured credentials.
debugTips: A 401 here is almost always credentials or an expired token, not the payload.
Correlate by correlation ID rather than by timestamp — retries make timestamps misleading.

stages.name: Middleware processing
stages.purpose: The integration platform validates, enriches and routes the message.
debugTips: Read the message-processing log before the target system's log — most failures are caught here first.

stages.name: Mapping
stages.purpose: Source fields are mapped to target fields. Unmapped source fields are dropped silently, which is why the Mapping Explorer flags them.

possibleErrors.title: Mapping could not resolve a field

debugTips: A field that arrives empty at the target is usually unmapped rather than empty at source.
Check the Mapping Explorer for MISSING and RENAMED links on this interface.

stages.name: Target system
stages.purpose: The ERP validates the document against its own master data and creates the sales order.
debugTips: These are master-data problems, not integration problems. Confirm the record exists in the target before changing any mapping.
Reproduce the same document manually in the target system — if it fails there too, the payload is not the cause.

stages.name: Acknowledgement
stages.purpose: The document number or the rejection is written back so the order reflects reality.
debugTips: An order stuck without a document number usually means the acknowledgement path failed, not the send.

flows.name: Price Import
flows.summary: A delimited price file is picked up and applied to commerce. Three stages, no middleware — this is what a file-only landscape actually looks like.

stages.name: File produced
stages.purpose: The source system exports current condition prices to a delimited file.
debugTips: Check the drop location and the file's timestamp before assuming the import failed — no file is a different problem from a bad file.

stages.name: Transfer
stages.purpose: The file lands on the shared location commerce polls.
debugTips: A partial file usually means the producer wrote in place instead of writing to a temporary name and renaming.

stages.name: Import job
stages.purpose: A scheduled job parses each row, validates it and writes the price. Partial success is normal: bad rows are rejected individually.

possibleErrors.title: Header does not match a known attribute

debugTips: A 'no column found' error is a header mismatch: compare the file's header row against the import mapping, not against the database.
Check the rejected-row report before re-running — a re-run repeats the same rejections.

flows.name: Invoice
flows.summary: Invoice headers and PDF documents are read on demand for the account area.

stages.name: Request invoices
stages.purpose: The account area asks for invoices for an order or a date range.

stages.name: Query target
stages.purpose: The query is forwarded to the ERP's invoice service.

possibleErrors.title: Service metadata does not match the client

debugTips: An EDMX mismatch after a target upgrade is a contract change, not a bug — regenerate the client metadata.

stages.name: Fetch document
stages.purpose: The rendered invoice document is retrieved as a binary.
debugTips: An invoice header without a document usually means the document has not been rendered in the target yet.

flows.name: Customer Sync
flows.summary: Customer and business partner records are kept aligned between the ERP and commerce.

stages.name: Change event
stages.purpose: The ERP emits a customer or partner change.

stages.name: Transform
stages.purpose: The change document is mapped to the commerce integration object structure.

stages.name: Persist
stages.purpose: The inbound integration object validates and writes the record.
debugTips: A unique-constraint failure here usually means the same record arrived twice, not that the data is wrong.

flows.name: Product Sync
flows.summary: Product master data is imported into the commerce catalogue.

stages.name: Feed produced
stages.purpose: The source system exports the product feed.

stages.name: Import
stages.purpose: Rows are applied to the catalogue and staged for approval.
debugTips: Catalogue version errors are configuration, not data — confirm the target catalogue and version exist for this environment.

stages.name: Index
stages.purpose: Updated products are re-indexed so search and listings reflect the change.
debugTips: A product correct in the backoffice but missing from search means the import worked and the index did not.

flows.name: Shipment
flows.summary: Delivery and tracking status is read for dispatched orders.

stages.name: Request status
stages.purpose: Commerce asks for delivery status for an order.

stages.name: Query target
stages.purpose: The query reaches the ERP delivery service.

flows.name: Pricing
flows.summary: A basket is priced in real time by the ERP. Direct, synchronous, and on the critical path — latency here is felt by every shopper.

stages.name: Basket priced
stages.purpose: Commerce needs authoritative prices including customer-specific conditions.

stages.name: Call target
stages.purpose: The pricing service is called directly, with no middleware in between.
debugTips: Because this is synchronous and on the critical path, a slow target is a slow storefront. Check the timeout budget before the payload.
Confirm there is a fallback price source — a hard failure here should degrade, not blank the basket.

flows.name: Returns
flows.summary: A return request is raised against a delivered order.

stages.name: Return requested
stages.purpose: A customer or agent raises a return for delivered items.

stages.name: Send to target
stages.purpose: The request is routed to the ERP returns process.

flows.name: Inventory
flows.summary: Stock levels are published as events and applied to commerce.

stages.name: Stock event
stages.purpose: The ERP publishes a stock change.

stages.name: Broker
stages.purpose: The event is retained on a topic for independent consumers.
debugTips: Stale availability with no errors is usually consumer lag, not a failed message.

stages.name: Apply
stages.purpose: Commerce applies the new level and invalidates availability caches.

links.notes: Present in the DTO but no middleware mapping exists, so the target receives nothing. This is the failure mode that reaches production silently.
Target renamed this field in its latest release; the mapping still uses the old name.
Commerce sends this but nothing consumes it. Harmless today; misleading when someone assumes it arrives.

mappingSets.name: Price file → Price row
mappingSets._comment: Two layers, because that is genuinely all there is. A file-based mapping does not have a DTO or a middleware hop, and padding it out to five columns would be a lie.

links.notes: New column in the latest feed version. No importer handles it yet, so it is ignored on every run.
Column removed by the producer. The importer still expects it, which is what raises 'no column found'.
Source widened this field; commerce still truncates at the old length.

apis.name: Commerce Web Services (OCC)
apis.description: The storefront-facing REST API. Any change to its contract is felt directly by the storefront.

operations.name: Get cart
operations.summary: Returns the current cart with entries and totals.

operations.name: Add to cart
operations.summary: Adds a product to the cart.

operations.name: Place order
operations.summary: Converts the cart into an order.

apis.name: Sales order service
apis.description: The target system's sales order creation contract.

operations.name: CreateSalesOrder
operations.summary: Creates a sales order from a commerce order.

apis.name: Billing document service
apis.description: OData service exposing billing documents and their rendered PDFs.

samplePayloads.name: SalesOrderRequest.xml
samplePayloads.description: Illustrative outbound order payload showing the envelope, header and one item.
samplePayloads.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<SalesOrderRequest xmlns="urn:example:sales:v1">
  <Header>
    <Reference>ORD-100482</Reference>
    <SoldToParty>C-4471</SoldToParty>
    <ShippingCondition>02</ShippingCondition>
    <Currency>USD</Currency>
    <RequestedDeliveryDate>2026-08-14</RequestedDeliveryDate>
    <ShipTo>
      <Street>120 Innovation Way</Street>
      <City>Indianapolis</City>
      <PostalCode>46204</PostalCode>
      <Country>US</Country>
    </ShipTo>
  </Header>
  <Items>
    <Item>
      <LineNumber>10</LineNumber>
      <Material>MAT-88213</Material>
      <Quantity unit="EA">4</Quantity>
      <NetPrice>128.50</NetPrice>
      <Plant>1010</Plant>
    </Item>
  </Items>
</SalesOrderRequest>

samplePayloads.description: The acknowledgement returned after a successful create.

samplePayloads.name: SalesOrderFault.xml
samplePayloads.description: A representative SOAP fault for a master-data rejection.
samplePayloads.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <soap:Fault>
      <faultcode>soap:Server</faultcode>
      <faultstring>Material MAT-88213 not maintained for plant 1010</faultstring>
      <detail>
        <ErrorCode>MATERIAL_NOT_FOUND</ErrorCode>
        <Field>Item/Material</Field>
      </detail>
    </soap:Fault>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>

_comment_discovery: These rules are what turn 'someone edited OrderExportConverter.java' into 'the outbound order interface is impacted' without asking a model. Highest priority wins, and every rule carries the evidence string shown to the user.

discoveryRules.evidence: Order conversion logic determines what reaches the outbound order payload; a change here can add or silently drop a field.
This type is part of the outbound order contract.
Invoice retrieval logic.
Shipment and delivery tracking logic.
Pricing is synchronous and on the storefront critical path, so a change here is felt by every shopper.
Returns processing logic.
Customer material info record resolution.
Integration object definitions describe the inbound contract; a change alters what commerce will accept.
Price import mapping — the header line here must match the feed's columns exactly.
Product import mapping.
An ImpEx script participates in file-based import; which feed it serves could not be determined from the path alone.
The type system is the floor of the platform: a model change propagates to every payload, mapping and import that touches the affected type.
Bean definitions generate the DTOs used by both the API layer and outbound payload construction.
OCC is the storefront-facing contract; a change here is visible to every client of the API.
A WSDL is a published contract; changing it changes what every consumer must send.
Schema definitions gate payload validation; a stricter schema rejects payloads that used to pass.
OData metadata defines the client's view of the service; a mismatch surfaces at runtime, not at build time.
Scripts frequently carry integration transformation logic, but which interface this one serves could not be determined from the path.
XSLT transforms payload structure directly.
A delimited file changed. If this is a feed sample, its header must stay aligned with the import mapping.
Endpoint and destination configuration decides where messages actually go; a wrong value here fails at runtime in the target environment only.
